text: Name a model whose name ends in Net
note: Name ends in 'net' (hyphen optional). Versions and sizes are aliases; NetV2 and Net++ successors are separate. Datasets like ImageNet allowed. Not 'Network'.

answers.q: Ciresan & Schmidhuber's GPU CNN won four contests from 2011, a year before AlexNet, with superhuman traffic-sign accuracy.
A dataset, not a model. It is the answer everyone reaches for first, so we'll allow it.
Each layer feeds every later layer. CVPR 2017 best paper.
He et al., 2015: learn a residual and add the input back. 152 layers, and first place at ILSVRC 2015.
Two GTX 580s, ReLU and dropout: ImageNet top-5 error of 15.3% in 2012, against 26% for the runner-up.
LeCun's digit reader. By the late '90s it was reading 10-20% of US checks.
Built for cell segmentation in 2015; later the workhorse inside diffusion models.
Simonyan & Zisserman, 2014: nothing but 3x3 convolutions, 16 or 19 layers deep, about 138M parameters.
The capital L salutes LeNet. The 22-layer Inception design won ILSVRC 2014 with about 12x fewer parameters than AlexNet.
Howard et al., 2017: depthwise separable convolutions plus a width multiplier, for phones.
Compound scaling: grow depth, width and resolution together with one coefficient.
DeepMind, 2016: dilated causal convolutions generating raw audio one sample at a time.
Qi et al., 2017: a shared MLP plus max-pooling, so the order of a point cloud's points doesn't matter.
AlexNet-level accuracy with 50x fewer parameters, under 0.5 MB compressed.
Grouped 1x1 convolutions, then a channel shuffle so the groups can talk.
Squeeze-and-excitation channel attention. Won the final ImageNet challenge in 2017.
Inverted residuals and linear bottlenecks.
Blocks found by architecture search, plus squeeze-and-excitation and hard-swish.
Permutation language modeling on Transformer-XL; it beat BERT on 20 tasks in 2019.
Encoder-decoder segmentation that upsamples by reusing the encoder's max-pooling indices.

aka: Focal Loss for Dense Object Detection
answers.q: A plain one-stage detector made competitive by focal loss (Lin et al., 2017).
Google, 2015: triplet-loss face embeddings; 99.63% on LFW.
Zou & Hastie, 2005: the one Net here with no neurons. Lasso and ridge penalties together.
Zhang & Agrawala, 2023: a trainable copy of Stable Diffusion's encoder, wired in with zero-initialized convolutions.
Zeiler and Fergus visualized AlexNet's features and retuned it. Their Clarifai entry won ILSVRC 2013.
Wider, not deeper: a 16-layer WRN beat thousand-layer ResNets.
Hinton's capsules, routed by agreement instead of max pooling.
Google's tabular network: sequential attention picks which features each decision step looks at.
Found by reinforcement-learning architecture search on 500 GPUs.
Joseph Redmon's YOLO backbone, named after his own C framework.
Two papers share the name: objects as center points, and keypoint triplets.
PointNet applied hierarchically, so it can see local structure. Counts under the 'Net++' rule.
Milletari et al., 2016: a 3D, residual U-Net with a Dice loss for volumetric segmentation.
'No new Net': a self-configuring U-Net pipeline that quietly wins most medical segmentation challenges.
Radosavovic et al.: design the design space, and the good widths follow a simple linear rule.
Fused-MBConv and progressive learning make it train up to 11x faster than EfficientNet.
Practical guidelines: judge a network by speed on the device, not by FLOPs.
Mobile Neural Architecture Search: optimizes measured latency on a Pixel phone, not FLOPs.
Makes cheap 'ghost' feature maps from a few real ones.
Evolved, not designed: found by regularized (aging) evolution.
Normalizer-Free: no BatchNorm, adaptive gradient clipping instead.
Scaled kernels up to 31x31 and found big kernels were worth it after all.
Keeps a high-resolution branch alive through the whole network.
BN and ReLU before the conv, and a 1001-layer ResNet that still trains.
Spatial pyramid pooling lets a CNN eat any image size and gave R-CNN a big speedup.
AlexNet with pooling and normalization swapped, straight from Caffe's model zoo.
Stanford, 2017: a 121-layer DenseNet trained on chest X-rays, claimed radiologist-level pneumonia detection.
Detects boxes as a pair of corner keypoints, with no anchors.
Adds a bottom-up path to FPN; it was the backbone of the winning COCO 2017 instance-segmentation entry.
Turns LiDAR point clouds into voxels with a learned feature encoder, end to end.
First CNN to learn optical flow end to end, trained on flying chairs.
Pyramid, warping and cost volume in one small optical-flow network.
Kendall et al., 2015: regress the camera's 6-DoF pose straight from a single image.
Defferrard et al., 2016: spectral graph convolution via fast Chebyshev polynomial filters.
Continuous-filter convolutions over interatomic distances for molecules.
Message passing that uses bond angles, via spherical Bessel and harmonic bases.
A lexical database, not a model. It also gave ImageNet its category tree.
Google swapped self-attention for a Fourier transform and kept about 92-97% of BERT's accuracy.
Microsoft's Retentive Network: attention swapped for retention, so it trains in parallel and infers as an RNN.
Microsoft's 1-bit LLMs: weights of just {-1, 0, 1}, about 1.58 bits each.
OpenAI's 2019 GPT-2-style music model: ten instruments, any style.
Animate Anyone's twin U-Net that injects a reference image's appearance into the video model.
Binary weights and activations, so convolutions become XNOR plus popcount.
Exploration by learnable parametric noise in the weights, instead of epsilon-greedy.
Planning in a learned latent dynamics model, from pixels only.
DeepMind: evolve which pathways through a giant network each task is allowed to train.
Luo & Mesgarani: speech separation on raw waveforms, skipping the spectrogram.
TasNet with a stack of dilated convolutions; it beat the ideal time-frequency mask on speaker separation.
A 1D U-Net on raw audio for source separation.
Microsoft's dilated attention: scales sequences to one billion tokens.
Prunes filters of the next layer by whether they matter to that layer's output.
Hierarchical residual-like connections inside a single block, for multi-scale features.
A GPU-friendly ResNet variant from Alibaba (Ridnik et al.).
A DenseNet that learns to prune its own group connections during training.
Ultra-deep without residuals, built from self-similar fractal blocks.
Very deep with no skip connections, thanks to a Dirac-delta weight parameterization.
Mixes several kernel sizes inside one depthwise convolution.
A DenseNet variant built to run real-time detection on phones.

aka: Working Hard to Know Your Neighbor's Margins

answers.q: Early-exit classifier: easy images leave early, hard ones go through the full net.
Learns per input which residual blocks to skip.
Huawei's 2023 minimalist CNN: no shortcuts, no attention, just a few layers.
Rewrite the Stars: element-wise multiplication, not width, does the heavy lifting.
Parallel subnetworks: 12 layers deep and still around 80% on ImageNet.
Reversible residual blocks: activations are recomputed on the way back, not stored.
A fully invertible ImageNet classifier: no information is discarded anywhere.
Classifies ImageNet from a bag of small local patches, ignoring where they sit.
Blocked local self-attention with haloed neighbouring blocks.
Swap the last three 3x3 convs of a ResNet for self-attention.
A tiny keyword-spotting ResNet that broadcasts 1D features across the frequency axis.
A real-time segmentation net with an initial block that downsamples fast.
A U-Net with a pretrained VGG11 encoder; it won Kaggle's Carvana masking challenge.
Two chained U-Nets form an autoencoder for unsupervised image segmentation.
Pairs a U-Net with an over-complete 'Ki-Net' that upsamples first, to catch tiny structures.
A U-Net made of U-Net blocks, for salient object detection; it powers many background-removal tools.

aka: Bottom-up Object Detection by Grouping Extreme Points

answers.q: Won VOT 2015 tracking by training on many videos with per-video domain-specific layers.
A Siamese network that learns both patch features and the similarity metric (Han et al., 2015).
Image restoration with no nonlinear activations at all: simple gating does the job.
NVIDIA's end-to-end driving CNN: pixels in, steering angle out.
Waymo's imitation-learning driver, trained on mid-level scene rasters with synthesized perturbations.
Waymo's polyline encoder for HD maps and agent trajectories.
Trajectory prediction as classification over a fixed set of trajectories.
Berkeley's grasp planner, trained on millions of synthetic point clouds with analytic grasp metrics.
Atomwise, 2015: the first deep CNN for structure-based drug discovery, run over 3D voxel grids of binding sites.
Folds a time series into a 2D image by its periods, then applies Inception-style 2D convolutions.
Gradient boosting where each weak learner is a small neural network.
Few-shot learning by learning the comparison, not just the embedding.
DeepMind's dilated-convolution seq2seq with linear-time translation.
Microsoft's DeepNorm let Transformers train to 1,000 layers.
DeepMind's net that learns how many steps to think before it answers.
Chen, Goodfellow & Shlens: grow a trained net wider or deeper without losing what it learned.
Trains with low-bit weights, activations and even gradients.
Convolutions with no multiplications: the filter is matched to each patch by L1 distance.
Zero-FLOP spatial convolutions: the shift just moves channels around.
Lotter, Kreiman & Cox: predictive coding for video, where each layer predicts and passes up only its errors.
Google Magenta's counterpoint by convolution: its Bach chorale doodle was the 2019 Doodle.
Valin and Skoglund: classic linear prediction inside a neural vocoder, real-time speech on one CPU core.
Picks seismic P and S wave arrival times with a U-Net.
Learns the cutoff frequencies of band-pass filters directly on raw waveforms.
A dataset of 3D CAD models, not a model. It is allowed.
A 3D CAD dataset, not a model; every point cloud paper reports it.
A dataset of annotated RGB-D indoor scans, not a model.
A commonsense knowledge graph, not a model.
A video benchmark of untrimmed human activities, not a model.
